# Backbone matrix

<!-- Generated by load/publish_matrix.sh. Do not edit by hand. -->

How the event backbone ([ADR-0070](../adr/0070-pluggable-event-backbone.md)) changes the numbers of the
[load harness](index.md): every scenario on the Native backbone (Phoenix.PubSub + Oban on Postgres) and on Kafka,
with one and three nodes. The `backbone` rows are the backbone zero-loss check: every activity of the run is
published to the backbone, and a platform webhook subscriber must observe each one exactly once.

Measured by the nightly `Load` workflow on GitHub's `ubuntu-24.04` runners (2026-10-15, commit `08bcd153c4fd`, profile `full`).


Commit `08bcd153c4fd`, 2026-10-15T02:25:35Z, profile `full`. Generated by `load/run.sh` (see [Benchmarks](index.md)).

### Setup

- **1 node, kafka**: 4 vCPU and 15.6 GiB visible to Docker (Linux, GitHub Actions 1000004864, kernel 6.17.0-1022-azure, Docker 28.0.4); per-node limits CPU unlimited, memory unlimited; Postgres 17.11, 159.9 MiB after the run; pool size 20 + 10 background; mock provider latency 20+10 ms, error rate 0.
  - `e2e`: conversations=100, subscribers_per_conversation=10, sockets=1000, rate_per_conversation=1, duration_s=60
  - `webhook_burst`: rate=500, duration_s=30, participants=200, targets=3
  - `idle`: sockets=10000, sockets_per_vu=200, connect_rate=100, ramp_s=100, hold_s=60
  - `reconnect_storm`: mode=storm, conversations=100, subscribers_per_conversation=10, sockets=1000, rate_per_conversation=1, duration_s=60, storm_at_s=15, storm_every_s=15
  - `rolling_restart`: mode=restart, conversations=100, subscribers_per_conversation=10, sockets=1000, rate_per_conversation=1, duration_s=70, storm_at_s=null, storm_every_s=null

  - `backbone`: backbone=kafka, subscriber=platform webhook (activity.created)
